title: normalize-origin-project-header-and-signed-session-nonce-for-streaming-toolcalls
author: Marina Cortez
description: Motivation: streaming stability and tool/function caller compatibility have regressed intermittently when proxied headers or nonstandard auth tokens are present. This PR standardizes the project/org identification headers, introduces a minimal signed-session nonce header for streaming toolcalls, and makes the compatibility layer with OpenAI semantics more robust without breaking existing clients. What this changes: 1) Adds normalization for Origin-Project and X-Project-ID headers so requests that include either header are treated identically by routing and access checks. 2) Introduces X-RW-Signed-Session header semantics: a compact base64 URL-safe token that contains a session id, short expiry, and a signature over connection-specific metadata. The server validates the signature and timestamp before accepting long-lived streaming frames or tool/function call handshakes. 3) Adds a lenient parser for Authorization: Bearer tokens that accepts both project-prefixed tokens (proj_...) and org-scoped tokens (org_...) and emits a standard internal principal header for downstream services. 4) Streaming frame guard rails: enforce header-level nonce validation on first chunk and reject connections that provide mismatched nonce between initial HTTP handshake and the first stream frame. 5) CORS: expose Origin-Project header via Access-Control-Expose-Headers to avoid browser-side blind spots for clients that rely on project-scoped keys. 6) OpenAI-compat: keep the Authorization Bearer behavior but ensure we do not accept legacy nonce in query params unless a feature flag is enabled. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for 2 weeks in hosted, gradual ramp to Dedicated, telemetry added to measure rejected nonces and header normalization frequency. Backwards compatibility: deprecated legacy query-nonce but still accepted if feature flag enabled; project header aliasing preserves current clients. Testing: unit tests for header normalization, integration tests for streaming handshake and toolcall signer, e2e regression harness running with OpenAI-compatible clients. Notes: this is focused on API surface and request/handshake semantics only, not on telemetry retention or KMS key rotation for signing tokens.
commits: feat(auth): add X-RW-Signed-Session validator and signer
chore(tests): add streaming handshake integration tests
docs(api): document header semantics and rollout notes
ci: add e2e flagged pipeline stage for nonce regression tests
review_comments: Ben Liu: The Signed-Session format looks compact and reasonable. Please add a short TTL constant and a test that simulates clock skew between signer and validator.
Marina Cortez: Added ttl constant and a test for 90s skew. Also added clear error codes for invalid signature vs expired.
Rajesh Gupta: We should be careful exposing Origin-Project to browsers. Confirm that we only echo it when the requestOrigin matches the allowedOrigins list.
Marina Cortez: Confirmed. CORS change gated by same allowlist check and only exposed for matching origins. Added unit tests.
Hannah Kim: CI flake on the e2e pipeline failed once, reran and passed. Approving once CI is green.
Marina Cortez: Fixed a deterministic race in the test harness by stubbing the clock. Re-ran CI pipeline.
QA: Verified streaming toolcall handshake with OpenAI-compat client and with Redwood SDK. No regression observed.
Security: Request signing code reviewed; signature uses HMAC-SHA256 with KMS keys and short TTL. Recommend rotation note in changelog.
merge_outcome: squash and merge; commit message: normalize Origin-Project header and add X-RW-Signed-Session nonce for streaming/toolcalls. Feature-flagged rollout and tests added.
release_notes: - Normalize Origin-Project/X-Project-ID headers so clients using either header are routed and authorized the same way. - Add X-RW-Signed-Session header for safer streaming and tool/function call handshakes. - Authorization Bearer parsing extended to accept project- and org-prefixed tokens while emitting a standard internal principal header. - CORS will now expose the Origin-Project header for allowed origins to improve browser integration. - Feature-flagged rollout with telemetry to monitor rejected nonces and header aliasing rate.
